description: System startup, shutdown, service, security subsystem, and operating-system state events.

source.note: Some of these events appear in the System log rather than Security — display channel alongside event ID.

1100.headline: The event log service shut down
1100.plain_english: The Windows event log service stopped. This usually happens during a normal shutdown. If it happens during normal operation, the log is no longer being written — a sign of tampering or a serious problem.
1100.technical_description: System event 1100: the event logging service has shut down.

where.Computer: Machine whose event log service stopped

1100.why_it_matters: Stopping the log service is a defence-evasion technique.
what_to_do: Confirm whether a system shutdown/restart was expected
If not, investigate — logs after this point will be missing
1100.important_note: Look for missing logs after 1100 — attacker-triggered stops often precede log clears.

1107.headline: The event log service encountered an error
1107.plain_english: The Windows event log service hit an error. Some events may be missing as a result.
1107.technical_description: System event 1107: the event logging service encountered an error.
1107.why_it_matters: Errors can cause gaps in the audit trail.
normal_when: Disk space issue or known bug
what_to_do: Check for log corruption or disk space
1107.important_note: Correlate with 1108 to identify missing events.

1108.headline: The event log service had an error processing a message
1108.plain_english: The Windows event log service had an error while processing a specific event — that event may not have been recorded correctly.
1108.technical_description: System event 1108: the event logging service encountered an error processing a message.
1108.why_it_matters: Some events may be missing or malformed.
1108.important_note: Indicates gap in the audit record.

4608.headline: Windows started
4608.plain_english: The Windows security subsystem started. Marks the beginning of a Windows session — useful for establishing a timeline.
4608.technical_description: Security event 4608: Windows started (security subsystem initialised).
4608.why_it_matters: Establishes a timeline for post-boot events.

severity.high: Reboot correlated with suspicious activity (e.g. tampering then reboot)

4614.headline: A notification package was loaded
4614.plain_english: Windows loaded a notification package (used for alerts or monitoring). Usually routine during startup.
4614.technical_description: Security event 4614: a notification package was loaded by the LSA.

severity.high: Unfamiliar package plus other suspicious changes

6144.headline: Security policy from Group Policy was applied successfully
6144.plain_english: Group Policy successfully applied a security policy to this computer. Routine and reassuring — the expected configuration is in place.
6144.technical_description: Security event 6144: security policy in Group Policy objects was applied successfully.

where.Computer: Machine where the policy was applied

6144.why_it_matters: Confirms that expected security policy is in effect.
what_to_do: No action needed if timing is expected

6145.headline: Security policy processing had errors
6145.plain_english: Group Policy had errors applying security policy to this computer. Some expected security settings may not be in effect — investigate.
6145.technical_description: Security event 6145: one or more errors occurred while security policy was processed.
6145.why_it_matters: Missing policy can leave the machine less protected than intended.
suspicious_when: Errors on a machine that should be fully managed
what_to_do: Check that expected GPOs are applied (gpresult)
Escalate if policy can't be applied

severity.high: Critical security policy failed to apply

6145.important_note: Failing GPOs are a real risk — the machine may be missing protections.

implementation_notes.verified_field: Only display a plain-English explanation when `verified` is true.
